Title & Venue & Year: REPLICANT: Learning Policies for Evading and Hardening Malware Detectors | arXiv preprint | 2026
Threat Model: Black-Box (Strict hard-label black-box: attacker receives only binary label clf(s_t) in {0, 1}, zero confidence scores or model internals; white-box variant REPLICANT_WB with continuous score deltas used for adversarial training)
Attacker Architecture: Hierarchical PPO Deep Reinforcement Learning Pipeline: (1) Feature Extractor encodes APK into binary vector s_t in X across Drebin, APIGraph, or RAMDA spaces; (2) Shared MLP Encoder (2 layers, 512 neurons, LeakyReLU, dropout) feeding three heads: (i) Query Head over {SUBMIT, MODIFY}, (ii) Masked Modify Head over capability set C, (iii) Critic Head estimating V(s_t); (3) Action Masking filters out no-ops, class conflicts, and budget violations; (4) Periodic Submits forced every p=10 steps with lambda_PS=0; (5) Problem-space Gadget Transplantation adds benign code fragments; (6) AT-REPLICANT 15-round adversarial hardening.
Manager Architecture & Policy: Query Policy (Higher-level): Shared MLP encoder (2 layers, 512 units, LeakyReLU, dropout) connected to Query Head (512 units) outputting probability distribution over discrete actions q_t in {SUBMIT, MODIFY}. Decides when to query target detector vs when to accumulate internal mutations. Masked to force periodic submits every p=10 steps (lambda_PS=0) and masked against consecutive submits without intermediate modifications.
Worker Architecture & Policy: Modify Policy (Lower-level): Shared MLP encoder connected to Modify Head (512 units) over capability set C = {c_1, ..., c_N}. When q_t = MODIFY, selects capability c_mt: X -> X. Governed by Action Masking to eliminate no-ops, Java class conflicts, and budget violations (>3 permissions, >60 classes).
State Space Representation (s_t): Binary feature vector s_t in X representing the modified malware sample at step t (s_0 original). Features depend on evaluated space: Drebin (permissions, APIs, intents, hardware, network), APIGraph (semantic API clusters), or RAMDA. Target feedback is binary label clf(s_t) in {0, 1}.
State Dimensions: Drebin: d = 10,000 binary features; APIGraph: d = 11,912 binary features; RAMDA: d = 379 binary features (Section 4, Page 6).
Action Selection Mechanism: Hierarchical Two-Tier Selection: (1) Query Head selects q_t in {SUBMIT, MODIFY}; (2) If q_t = MODIFY, Modify Head selects capability c_mt in C; (3) Action Masking eliminates no-ops, Java class conflicts, and budget violations (>3 permissions, >60 classes); (4) Forced periodic submits every p=10 steps (lambda_PS=0). Capability set sizes: 3,143 for Drebin, 4,804 for APIGraph, 1,739 for RAMDA. During evaluation, selects argmax action.
Reward Formulation: Black-box MDP Reward (Eq. 4-6): R(s_t, q_t, m_t) = R_success = H = 100 if q_t = SUBMIT and clf(s_t)=0; R_detected = -1 if q_t = SUBMIT and clf(s_t)=1; R_modify(s_t, c_mt) = -1 if q_t = MODIFY. Forced submits scaled by lambda_PS = 0. White-box variant Reward (Eq. 7): R_WB(s_t, c_mt) = lambda_WB * (clf_score(s_t) - clf_score(s_{t+1})) with lambda_WB = 5.
Integrity & Functionality Verification: Semantics-preserving by construction: gadget transplantation adds only benign code (0 -> 1), leaving original malware logic completely intact (no 1 -> 0 deletions). Action masking prevents Java class conflicts and enforces per-gadget budgets (<= 3 permissions, <= 60 classes). Packaging and re-signing via Apktool/jarsigner. Evaluated on Hypercube dataset (224,965 apps).

Worker Architecture & Policy: N/A (No reinforcement learning Worker agent; low-level genetic operations within each population are Crossover [random parent gene swap], Mutation [add call, reduce call, exchange call], and Elitist Selection).
State Space Representation (s_t): Function Call Graph (FCG) G = (V, E) of the application. In Apoem, an individual in population P_i is represented as a set of added edges x_r^{(i, j)} = {e_1, ..., e_n}. For substitute GCN, node features are 2D degree vectors [in-degree, out-degree]. Target MaMaDroid represents FCG as 1st-order Markov transition probability matrix between packages or families.

Action Selection Mechanism: Multi-Population Co-Evolutionary Selection (Apoem, Alg. 1): (1) Candidate edge generation chooses non-leaf nodes (user-defined) as callers and leaf nodes (Android standard with public modifier and primitive/void/String args) as callees; (2) Three populations evolve in parallel; (3) Elitist selection retains top N individuals based on threat degree T and perturbation size L; (4) Cross-population immigration transfers genes fine-to-coarse and coarse-to-fine; (5) Crossover and 3-mode mutation update edge sets; (6) Try-Catch Trap inserts callee calls into Smali.
